selectionPolicy.description: 100 completed portrait/description pairs: 75 exact canonical identities with registry or breed-organization research paths and 25 recognized varieties. Ordered reserves replace genuine blocks only through append-only amendments. Exact references still require approval before calls.
selectionPolicy.historicalPolicy: No modern reconstruction of extinct identities. All 36 historical identities assessed and deferred.
selectionPolicy.crossbreedPolicy: 139 crossbreed identities assessed; named cross candidates remain reserves pending exact adult reference and primary evidence. No phenotype or temperament predictability inferred.
selectionPolicy.existingHoldPolicy: All 20 E holds retained without reopening; none selected. Remaining pack-engaged canonical discovery entries are held in E.

No unique intended morphology is established for this generic entry; choosing either subtype would silently resolve an unresolved catalog distinction. No sufficiently clear whole-adult morphology reference passed review. Three own-work originals were imported and inspected: Stella is wet, leaping, and shadowed; the 505x404 standing comparison places the small Murray in deep shadow at very low subject resolution; the 576x768 seated comparison gives a small head/chest view but conceals body length, hindquarters and tail. These may document the breed, but they do not support confident premium full-body synthesis of the distinct smaller Murray type. Three-dog file failed safe importer for missing reviewable creator; no bypass. Keep neutral fallback pending a clearer own-work adult original; do not substitute tall British Curly Coated Retriever.

Hold rather than substitute a generic Central Asian Shepherd or invent undocumented anatomy.

scene.description: A quiet Scottish upland pasture after light rain, with muted green grass, low heather and softly receding hills beneath an overcast bright sky. The Collie stands on a dry, level patch of short grass, head turned slightly toward the open valley.
scene.rationale: The FCI standard ties the Rough Collie to Scottish shepherd working stock, so open upland pasture evokes its history without depicting sheep, a handler or a staged working claim. Cool soft light preserves the sable-and-white coat texture and the dog stays fully separated from the landscape.

evidence.title: FCI standard No. 156: Collie (Rough)
evidence.evidence: FCI No. 156 describes friendly, happy, active temperament, a quick alert look when listening, Scottish shepherd working ancestry, shared recent Rough/Smooth ancestry despite coat length, and many dogs still capable of work; it also describes the low-carried tail, tipped ears, abundant mane and sable/white markings.
